blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Aeolian processes thrive in arid and semi-arid climates with high evaporation rates and minimal rainfall.
A lack of dense vegetation allows wind to easily erode and transport surface materials.
Continuous rock disintegration driven by large daily temperature ranges creates an abundance of loose sediments.
Strong, persistent winds serve as the primary dynamic force behind wind-driven erosion and deposition.

blocks.content: Large temperature range causing rock disintegration

items: Exams frequently ask for the primary climate conditions required for aeolian landform development (Arid/Semi-arid, High Evaporation, Low Rainfall).
Remember that thermal weathering (large temperature ranges) is the chief mechanical process supplying loose sediments for wind erosion in deserts.
